scheme_name: Operation of River Rafting / Kayaking Activities
description:
Operation of River Rafting and Kayaking Activities is an initiative launched by the Government of India to promote adventure tourism and enhance the livelihoods of local communities.

The scheme was officially launched in 2020 as part of the Ministry of Tourism's efforts to boost tourism in the country.

The initiative aims to develop and promote river rafting and kayaking as adventure sports in various river systems across India.

The primary objective is to create a sustainable tourism model that benefits local economies while preserving the natural environment.

The government seeks to increase the number of adventure tourism activities by 25 percent by the year 2025.

The scheme also aims to train local youth in river rafting and kayaking techniques to create job opportunities.

By 2025, the government targets to train at least 10,000 individuals in these adventure sports.

The benefits of this scheme include the promotion of local culture and heritage through adventure tourism.

Participants in the scheme can expect to receive training from certified instructors.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 100 crores for the development of infrastructure related to adventure sports.

This budget will be utilized for the construction of facilities such as training centers and equipment storage.

The scheme also includes the establishment of safety protocols to ensure the well-being of participants.

Local communities will benefit from increased tourism, which can lead to higher incomes.

The government estimates that the scheme could create approximately 50,000 direct and indirect jobs in the tourism sector.

Eligibility for participation in the training programs includes individuals aged between 18 and 35 years.

Participants must also possess a minimum educational qualification of 10th grade.

Income criteria for beneficiaries are set at a maximum annual income of INR 3 lakhs.

The application process for the scheme involves several steps.

Interested individuals must first visit the official website of the Ministry of Tourism.

They need to fill out an online application form with personal details and qualifications.

Required documents include proof of age, educational certificates, and income statements.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local tourism department.

Successful applicants will receive a confirmation email with details of the training schedule.

The training programs are conducted in various locations known for their river systems.

These locations include Rishikesh in Uttarakhand and the Teesta River in Sikkim.

Training sessions typically last for one month and include both theoretical and practical components.

Participants will learn about safety measures, equipment handling, and navigation techniques.

After successful completion of the training, participants will receive a certification.

This certification will enhance their employability in the adventure tourism sector.

The frequency of training programs is set to occur quarterly throughout the year.

Disbursement of funds for infrastructure development is scheduled to take place in phases.

The first phase of funding is expected to be released by March 2024.

Subsequent phases will depend on the progress of the initial phase.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India.

The Ministry collaborates with various state tourism departments to execute the program effectively.

Contact details for inquiries can be found on the official Ministry of Tourism website.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of environmental conservation.

Participants are educated on the ecological significance of rivers and responsible tourism practices.

The government aims to promote eco-friendly practices among adventure tourism operators.

Statistics indicate that adventure tourism has the potential to contribute significantly to India's GDP.

The sector is expected to grow at a CAGR of 20 percent over the next five years.

The initiative aligns with the government's broader vision of promoting 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' or self-reliant India.

By enhancing adventure tourism, the government aims to attract both domestic and international tourists.

The scheme is also expected to increase the visibility of lesser-known rivers and regions.

Local artisans and businesses will benefit from the influx of tourists.

The government plans to organize annual adventure sports festivals to showcase these activities.

These festivals will feature competitions and exhibitions to attract more participants.

The initiative is part of a larger strategy to diversify tourism offerings in India.

The government recognizes the potential of adventure sports to attract younger demographics.

The scheme also includes provisions for the development of marketing strategies to promote river rafting and kayaking.

Social media campaigns and collaborations with travel influencers are part of the marketing plan.

The government is also working on partnerships with private sector players to enhance training and infrastructure.

The initiative aims to create a robust ecosystem for adventure tourism in India.

By 2025, the government hopes to establish India as a premier destination for adventure sports.

The scheme is expected to foster community engagement and participation in tourism development.

Local communities will have a say in the management and operation of adventure tourism activities.

The government will provide support for the establishment of local cooperatives to manage these activities.

This cooperative model is designed to ensure that profits are distributed fairly among community members.

The scheme is also aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations.

By promoting responsible tourism, the government aims to protect natural resources for future generations.

The initiative is a significant step towards enhancing India's global standing in adventure tourism.

The government encourages feedback from participants to continuously improve the scheme.

Regular assessments and evaluations will be conducted to measure the impact of the initiative.

The scheme represents a commitment to developing a sustainable and inclusive tourism sector in India.
